question: Antibiotics are not indicated in uncomplicated acute viral rhinitis (common cold) because it is caused by viruses (predominantly rhinoviruses), and antibiotic use does not shorten illness duration but contributes to antimicrobial resistance.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. This statement is entirely true. Rhinoviruses and other respiratory viruses cause the common cold; antibiotics have no antiviral activity and are contraindicated unless a bacterial secondary complication (acute sinusitis, otitis media) develops.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Uncomplicated acute rhinitis is a self-limiting viral illness. Treatment is symptomatic (saline irrigation, decongestants if needed, analgesics). Prescribing antibiotics is one of the most common and harmful errors in primary care ENT — it does not help the patient and drives resistance.
